correctness.rationale: A 72-state complement quotient with two identical 16-state binary blocks and a transient nilpotent middle block gives denominator D(z)^2. The 16-state characteristic polynomial is reconstructed exactly by integer Newton identities. Each numerator has degree at most 41, and exact transfer coefficients through degree 42 determine N(z) identically. A separate direct full-word enumeration agrees through length 12. The asymptotic follows from the unique primitive recurrent component and a nonzero leading numerator at rho.

value.rationale: One unknown coordinate is a basic erasure uncertainty model in string constraints. The exact infinite length enumerator determines how every possible placement of one hole interacts with both period-two and period-three square checks; the nontrivial squared transfer denominator and positive n prefactor quantify the effect of a single erasure without changing the exponential constrained capacity. Neither a single numerical sample nor a reparametrized no-hole count.
